pool.text: Kraków became the seat of Polish monarchs from the Piast dynasty.
Bolesław V the Chaste incorporated the rebuilt city and introduced new trade privileges.
King Casimir founded the Jagiellonian University in central Europe.
Kasper Straube printed the Calendarium Cracoviense, the first work printed in Poland.
The famous church bell Zygmunt was cast by Hans Behem in Poland.
Sigismund III Vasa moved the administrative capital of the Commonwealth to Warsaw.
Kelly's book The Trumpeter of Krakow won a Newbery Award.
The Kraków Philharmonic was built as the principal concert hall.
The Germans arrested university professors and academics in Sonderaktion Krakau.
Soviet forces under Marshal Ivan Konev entered the city and began arrests.
Karol Wojtyła was elevated to the papacy as Pope John Paul II.
Kraków was named European Capital of Culture by the European Union.
Legislation introduced new rules for the election of the City Council.
Extensive excavations preceded the construction of the museum, continuing until a later year.
The Opera moved into its first permanent House in the autumn.
Extensive excavations that started years prior eventually continued until this year.
The UN Conference ranked Kraków as an emergent city location for BPO projects.
Kraków was officially approved as a City of Literature by authorities.
Kraków was awarded 1st place in the Top city-break destinations survey conducted by Which?
The city hosted World Youth Day during the summer months.
